purpose: This medicine is used to help your heart pump more effectively when it is not working as well as it should, a condition called heart failure. It is given through an IV in a hospital setting to give your heart a boost. It helps improve blood flow throughout your body so your organs get the oxygen they need.
how_it_works: Milrinone works by blocking a specific enzyme in your heart muscle called phosphodiesterase-3. By blocking this enzyme, it allows certain chemical signals to build up inside your heart cells, which makes your heart beat stronger and more efficiently. It also helps relax the blood vessels so your heart does not have to work as hard to push blood through your body.
common_side_effects: The most common side effect is an irregular or fast heartbeat (arrhythmia). You may also notice a drop in blood pressure, which can cause dizziness or lightheadedness. Headache is also fairly common. Less often, some people may experience chest pain or low platelet counts in the blood.
warnings: This medicine can cause serious irregular heart rhythms, so your heart will be closely monitored the entire time you receive it. It can also lower your blood pressure significantly, which may require adjustments to your treatment. If you have severe heart valve problems or very low blood pressure to begin with, this medicine may not be safe for you. Always tell your care team about all other medications you take, since some drugs can interact with milrinone.
typical_dosing: This medication is only given by healthcare professionals through an IV in a hospital or clinic. The usual starting dose is a slow loading infusion followed by a continuous drip at a rate adjusted to your specific needs, typically between 0.375 and 0.75 micrograms per kilogram of body weight per minute. Your doctor will adjust the dose based on how your heart responds and how your kidneys are working.
